newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian man killed in fight with foreign troops.
newsitem.headline: Albanian man killed in fight with foreign troops.

text.p: Greek troops, in Albania to help secure coming elections, shot and killed an Albanian man in a fight after he tried to sell them drugs, the multinational protection force said on Thursday.
"The man arrived dead at the local hospital," a spokesman for the Italian-led force said by telephone.

The incident on Wednesday night started when two men in a blue car approached guards at the main gate of the Greek troops' headquarters in Elbasan, central Albania, insistently proffering drugs to the soldiers, he said.
The sentries had refused the offers several times when one of the men took a Kalashnikov rifle from the car and started shooting in the air towards a nearby sentry, he said.
The Greek troops returned fire, also shooting in the air. Then shots from the Kalashnikov hit the guards' sandbags, and the men got into the car and drove away amid more shooting.
The troops' spokesman said the Greek commander had contacted local police who later informed them of the death of one of the men. He could give no more details.

The incident was the second significant intervention by foreign troops in Albania on Wednesday. Romanian troops in Girokaster, southern Albania, rescued 11 foreign election monitoring staff trapped by armed gangs in a restaurant.

A total of around 7,000 troops will be stationed in Albania to help protect Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) observers at the June 29 poll, amid mounting tension and lawlessness. Over 6,000 are already in the country.
The troops have orders to defend themselves and the OSCE observers if they come under attack.
Parts of this Balkan ex-Communist country have spun out of government control in riots and looting following the collapse of fraudulent investment schemes earlier this year.
